children: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told a key government council that recent wage growth was "quite strong" and aligned with the pace at which inflation will sustainably hit the central bank's 2% target, minutes of the council's meeting showed on Monday.

"It's desirable for wage and price growth to rise moderately together," Ueda was quoted as saying at the council's meeting held on November 11, adding the BOJ will guide policy to achieve such conditions in a sustainable fashion.

Next year's wage negotiations between companies and unions, as well as the extent to which firms will pass on rising labour costs through price hikes, will be among key factors in setting policy, Ueda said, according to the minutes.
The remarks came in response to a question by Toshihiro Nagahama, the key economic council's private-sector member who warned of recent weak signs in household income and consumption.

At the October 30 meeting, the BOJ kept interest rates steady at 1.25% but declared that underlying inflation has achieved its 2% target in a sign it would continue to push borrowing costs higher to combat inflation risks.
Ueda explained the BOJ's decision and policy stance at the council's meeting.

At the meeting, Nagahama said it was important to sustain a positive cycle of sustained wage and price growth, rather than aiming solely at pushing up prices — a view echoed by another panel member and former BOJ deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe.
Hand-picked by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to join the government council, both Nagahama and Wakatabe are known by markets as advocates of expansionary fiscal and monetary policy.
